title: Config document
description: config.yaml — the configuration surface an environment provides: which keys it declares and where their values come from. It never carries a secret value. Specified in framework/spec/kinds/environment.md; no portal code parses it.

$schema.description: The dialect discriminator (0015-artifact-dialects); the canonical value is this schema's own $id. Deliberately unpinned rather than const: a value naming some other dialect is W_ARTIFACT_DIALECT, a warning, read as the legacy dialect and never broken — a const here would restate that ruling as a hard rejection in the one place a severity cannot be relaxed. The loader strips the key once it has recorded the dialect, so nothing downstream ever sees it — including on the day something finally parses this file.

config.description: REQUIRED if the file exists. The whole top level: there is no environment-wide preamble and no grouping key, because a key's scope is carried by its own `for:` and nothing else.

^x-.description: The escape hatch reaches into this artifact, at the top level and inside entries. Tolerated and ignored by the portal; any other unknown key is E_ENV_CONFIG_SCHEMA. No top-level version: both environment siblings are part of the entity's version snapshot and carry no version field of their own.

entry.description: One declared key. Unique per (key, for) pair — a fact about the list, and therefore not statable here: uniqueItems compares whole entries, so two declarations of one key differing only in their description are distinct to a validator.

key.description: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE on purpose, and not kebab-case: config keys belong to the runtime's namespace, not to the catalog's. Env-var casing is what an operator copy-pastes, and it makes `grep -r DATABASE_URL solutions/` unambiguous against SRN segments, which are kebab-case by grammar.

for.description: The component or product the key applies to (E_ENV_TARGET_KIND). Absent means environment-wide. A `for:` naming a component that does not run in this environment is dead configuration, W_ENV_CONFIG_ORPHAN.

secret.description: Marks the value as sensitive. It is the discriminator between the two shapes an entry may take, and the only field here that changes which other fields are legal.

value.description: The literal value, for a key that has one in the open. FORBIDDEN when secret is true (E_ENV_SECRET_VALUE) — at any status, in any environment, because this file is reviewable in git and anything in it is public.

source.description: A locator for the value and never the value: vault:kv/acme/production/checkout#database-url. Free-form but stable. REQUIRED when secret is true.

description.description: One line: what the key controls.

then.description: The three-layer rule, stated where a schema can hold it: the contract lives in git, the declaration lives in git, and the value lives only in a vault or at deploy time. Keyed on `secret: true` rather than on the presence of `secret`, so an explicit `secret: false` is the ordinary shape and not a special case.

srn-ref.description: An ordinary SRN reference. Relative forms resolve against the artifact's own URI, srn://{solution}/environment/{name}/config.yaml, so the solution-absolute form is strongly preferred. An artifact suffix is refused (ENV11): `for:` names an entity, and an artifact has no kind.
